summary: The Dominican Republic admits tourists from the US, Canada, the UK, the EU and most of the Americas visa-free for 30 days (extendable up to 120), requires every traveler to complete the free digital e-Ticket form for both arrival and departure, and waives its visa entirely for anyone holding a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen multiple-entry visa or permanent residence.

The list of origin countries the requirement applies to is the Dominican Republic's own and differs from WHO's risk list.

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read publishes a minimum amount. Canada's travel advice says you may need to prove adequate funds for the duration of your stay when you enter, and give the address where you will be staying.

declarations.name: e-Ticket (digital entry and exit form)
declarations.submitWindow: Online, for arrival and again for departure
declarations.text: Every passenger entering or leaving the Dominican Republic must complete the digital e-Ticket, a form required by the Dirección General de Migración and the Dirección General de Aduanas. The Dirección General de Migración says the e-Ticket is free and that unofficial lookalike sites charge for it, so use only the official eticket.migracion.gob.do site.

source.name: Dirección General de Migración — E-TICKET, ticket electrónico de entrada y salida

currencyLimits.text: Cash of USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent in Dominican pesos or another currency) and bearer instruments must be declared to customs officers on entry or exit, using the form provided for that purpose, with documents showing that the money was lawfully obtained.

source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas — Manual del Viajero (traveller's guide)

payments.text: No official source we could read describes how widely cards are accepted in the Dominican Republic. Australia's Smartraveller warns that credit card and ATM fraud are common and advises using ATMs in daylight hours at hotels, shopping centres or other controlled areas.

safety.text: The UK government describes the crime rate as high, from bag-snatching and pickpocketing to violent crime and carjacking. It says thieves on motorcycles snatch bags from pedestrians and reach into cars stopped at red lights, and that assaults on foreigners have occurred, including at beach resorts. It advises avoiding remote areas, particularly after dark, and not wearing expensive jewellery or carrying large amounts of cash.

faq.question: What is the Dominican Republic e-Ticket and who needs it?
faq.answer: The e-Ticket is a free, mandatory digital form required by the Dirección General de Migración and the Dirección General de Aduanas. Every passenger entering or leaving the country must complete it, at the official site eticket.migracion.gob.do; Migration says lookalike sites charge for it.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the Dominican Republic?
faq.answer: No. US citizens enter visa-free as tourists for 30 days; when you arrive by air, the tourist card is included in your airline ticket, according to the Government of Canada. You need a valid passport and the free e-Ticket form. The UK government says a visit can be extended for a fee up to 120 days.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than 30 days in the Dominican Republic?
faq.answer: Yes. The Government of Canada says you can apply for an extension of up to 120 days at the Dirección General de Migración in Santo Domingo, after you arrive and before your tourist card expires, and that overstaying can lead to deportation or refusal of re-entry.

faq.question: Do I still need to buy a tourist card for the Dominican Republic?
faq.answer: The Government of Canada says that if you arrive by air, the cost of the tourist card is included in your airline ticket, and that if you arrive by sea you obtain the card at the point of entry from the Dirección General de Impuestos Internos. It says the e-Ticket does not replace the tourist card.

faq.question: Can I enter the Dominican Republic with a US, UK or Schengen visa instead of a Dominican visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Under Decree No. 691-07, nationals of visa-required countries (such as China, India, the Philippines or Vietnam) who hold permanent residence or a valid multiple-entry visa for the United States, the European Union (Schengen), Canada or the United Kingdom can enter for tourism with just a valid passport and a tourist card.
